clue.text: See 8
The Severn Bore's starting as rain falls around

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the one letter taken from the bore
rain that falls comes down jumbled, so these words are rearranged
only the opening letter of the word Bore's is used

explanation.surface: The tidal wave up the Severn begins as rain comes down all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' is the anagram signal, 'around' the container and 'starting' the first-letter pick. The Severn bore is a tidal wave that runs up England's River Severn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabrina is the nymph of the river in Milton's Comus and the old Latin name of Britain's longest river.

clue.text: Record turn in the lunar cycle

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a turn is an act on the variety stage

explanation.surface: A diary entry notes a change of course partway through the moon's phases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is a music-hall act, not a rotation. The definition is loose: the epact is a figure belonging to the lunar cycle, the moon's age at the start of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The epact is a term of calendar reckoning tied to the moon's cycle, the moon's age in days on 1 January.

clue.text: Potentially bad sign for the corporation

indicators.note: the word bad is potentially something else, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A warning that things may go badly for the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' rearranges BAD into ABD. 'Corporation' is an old British joke word for a pot belly, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is jocular old British slang for a large belly or paunch, the stomach region.

clue.text: See 8
Volatile girl one grabs in the market!

indicators.note: the word one grabs and holds the girl inside it

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, and sal volatile is smelling salts

explanation.surface: A flighty girl is snatched up by someone at the marketplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volatile girl' is SAL, a girl's name borrowed from sal volatile, the smelling salts.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods offered for purchase are on sale, available in the market.

clue.text: Agent surviving without pre-euro currency

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the surviving word encloses the currency

parts.note: something extant is still in existence
the ecu was the European currency unit before the euro

explanation.surface: An operative lives on without the old money of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a removal but means outside, as in old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An executant is one who carries out or performs something, a doer or agent.

clue.text: They admit mates to the masters' circle

definitions.text: They admit mates to the masters' circle

parts.words: They admit mates to the masters' circle
parts.note: read as passes that let one's friends through the gate into an exclusive gathering, such as the Masters golf tournament

explanation.definitionFit: Tickets are passes that admit their holders to an event or venue.

clue.text: Posh, his vice was her misfortune. That b__ song a mama's woe? C-could be!

annotationWithheld.why: Posh, his vice was her misfortune. That b__ song a mama's woe? C-could be! The anagram's 46 letters give the whole song SHE WAS POOR BUT SHE WAS HONEST VICTIM OF A RICH MANS GAME, but the file's group omits 11-across VICTIM, so the wordplay cannot give the group's 40 letters without six letters no clue word supplies separately.
annotationWithheld.clue: Posh, his vice was her misfortune. That b__ song a mama's woe? C-could be!

clue.text: The father of Waterloo?

parts.note: read as the creators of the pop song Waterloo, the Swedish group, whose name is also an Aramaic word for father

explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish band won Eurovision 1974 with Waterloo, and in Aramaic the word means father.

clue.text: Seed spilling, see! His need disturbed the Church

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are thrown out of order

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced like the word see
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a man's urgent want upset the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' signals the anagram. 'see' gives the letter C by its sound alone, a liberty the clue does not signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dehiscence is the bursting open of a seed pod or fruit to release its seeds, a botanical term.

clue.text: Two-man quarry

parts.note: Vic is a man's name
Tim is a second man's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-man' supplies two men's names side by side. The answer is also part of the long song at 8-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarry is a hunted creature, the prey or target of a pursuit.

clue.text: Morse's menage backing code with stratagems

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for code is read in reverse

parts.note: a law is a legal code
ruses are tricks or stratagems

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse's household supports secret codes and cunning plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is not the TV detective or the telegraph code but an old word for a walrus.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is an archaic name for the large tusked sea mammal, so a group of them is its household.

clue.text: Stardust is seen in some scanner by Protestant

indicators.note: the singer and the word is are seen inside the scanner

parts.note: a CT scanner is a kind of medical scanner
Alvin Stardust was a British glam-rock singer of the 1970s

explanation.surface: Stardust shows up on a hospital scanner next to a churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stardust' is the singer Alvin Stardust, so it gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Calvinist follows John Calvin's Reformed theology, a branch of Protestantism.

clue.text: Liberal taken in by pointless bloody self-approbation

parts.note: vain means futile or pointless

indicators.note: the Liberal is taken inside the words that follow

parts.note: gory means bloody

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is fooled by empty, gory self-satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Vainglory is excessive pride in oneself, boastful self-approval.

clue.text: See 8
Poet speaking of Psyche

indicators.note: speaking means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: the id is part of the psyche, so the phrase becomes of id

explanation.surface: A poet talking about the Greek heroine Psyche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Psyche' is not Cupid's lover but the mind, which gives ID; said aloud, OF ID gives the Roman poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses and the Art of Love.

clue.text: See 8
Ruthless order to setter on Korean diet?

definitions.text: order to setter on Korean diet?
definitions.meaning: a command to a setter, the gun dog, to dine as dogs are said to be eaten in Korea

explanation.surface: Telling a gun dog to follow a Korean menu is harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eat-dog world is one of ruthless, cut-throat competition.

clue.text: No harm in looking through it? On the contrary!

definitions.text: No harm in looking through it? On the contrary!

parts.words: No harm in looking through it? On the contrary!
parts.note: read as a gaze said to do great harm, the opposite of an innocent glance

explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent look believed to cast a curse on its victim.

clue.text: Seat raised bearing a device

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: N, north, is a compass bearing
a motto is a heraldic device on a coat of arms

explanation.surface: A chair hoisted up carries a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the whole of N, A and MOTTO upwards. 'device' looks like a gadget but is a heraldic motto.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a low padded seat or footstool without a back.

clue.text: Remove Oxford United? No, he's reunited!

parts.note: U is short for United in team names

indicators.note: the words no and he's are reunited in a new order

parts.note: taken as its letters

explanation.surface: Should Oxford United be removed? No, the player is back with the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' is the shoe, not the city or its football club; 'reunited' rearranges NO HES into NSHOE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxford is a laced leather shoe, so taking one off is to unshoe.

clue.text: Carter's wit, hopeless case

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit
a goner is someone beyond help

explanation.surface: The humour of a man named Carter has no hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carter' looks like a surname but is one who drives a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggoner drives a wagon, just as a carter drives a cart.

clue.text: Wholly enthusiastic without books

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the keen word goes round the books

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Completely keen while having no reading matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a removal but means outside, as in old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means entirely or as a whole.

clue.text: Woods imitated at Harfleur?

definitions.meaning: in Henry V before Harfleur the king urges his men to imitate the action of this big cat

explanation.definitionFit: The golfer is Tiger Woods, and Shakespeare's Henry tells his troops to imitate the action of the striped cat.

clue.text: ie sloop hut constructed for steersman's comfort

indicators.note: something constructed is built from parts, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A hut on a boat is built to keep the helmsman snug.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilothouse is the enclosed wheelhouse sheltering the helmsman on a vessel.

clue.text: See 8
Amazon in retreat from the Old Man's island

parts.note: the Old Man of Hoy is a sea stack off the Orkney island of Hoy
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A warrior woman withdrawing from an old fellow's island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' is not the river but a boisterous woman. The Old Man of Hoy is a famous rock pillar in Orkney, off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoyden is a boisterous, unruly girl, a tomboy; an amazon is a strong, assertive woman.

clue.text: Abraham's tomb here in the Bronx

indicators.note: the place sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Abraham is buried in a New York borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebron, in the West Bank, holds the Cave of the Patriarchs where Abraham is said to be buried.
